entities.summary:
Lucius Aemilius Mamercinus Privernas was a Roman statesman who served as consul in 341 and 329 BC, Magister Equitum in 342, Dictator in 335 and 316, and Interrex in 326. As the son of Lucius Aemilius Mamercinus, a prominent aristocrat, Privernas was born into a wealthy and influential family. This privileged upbringing likely shaped his career ambitions and political allegiances. His rise to power was marked by his service in the Roman Republic's military, where he demonstrated bravery and strategic prowess.

Privernas' most notable achievements include his role in the Samnite Wars and his efforts to reform the Roman calendar. His legacy extends beyond his own time, as his policies and decisions had far-reaching consequences for the Roman state and its expansion into Italy.

Despite his significant contributions to Roman history, Privernas' personal life remains somewhat of a mystery. Little is known about his family, relationships, or even his exact birthdate. However, it is clear that he played a crucial role in shaping the course of Roman politics and society.

In the end, Privernas' life was cut short when he died in 350 BCE at the age of 45. His death marked the end of an era in Roman politics, and his successors would have to navigate the complex web of alliances and rivalries that he had carefully crafted.
